newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end up on select foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end up on select foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Wednesday on select foreign buying of plantation and tobacco stocks, brokers said.

The all share index closed 2.72 points up at 622.82. Price gains outnumbered losses by 17 to 11. Blue chip Ceyon Tobacco Co Ltd rose three rupees to 35 while Bogawantalawa Plantations Ltd rose 1.25 rupees to 33.25.
"Foreign investors see good future growth in the plantation sector, which did very well in both 1995 and 1996," said Dihan Dedigama, a trader at brokerage John Keells.
Overall market conditions were quiet with many investors marking time until the March 21 local government elections, brokers said.
"There were a few small retail investors trying to buy low-valued shares which they expect to rise after the election," said Seedantha Kulatilleke, a trader at Allied Phillips Securities.
Investors are on the sidelines ahead of the election due to fears of violence which could depress prices, he said.
